title: Second marriage, children and family life
summary: Leeman talks about his wife Irene, their children and the loss of a daughter at 17; he and Hinton praise their wives and the family life Leeman always wanted.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: That was your first marriage. Now you had a second marriage, right? You did have a second marriage.
The latest is with you now, this lovely lady which we all know, and is almost as popular in the music business as you are.
We had our 28th anniversay last week.
And we had three children. We have Chris who is 26, and my daughter Nancy is 21. And we lost, 7 years ago, we lost a daughter.
Right, and we sadly remember that.
The reason I'm here with you is because of our close relationship, and our deep respect for each other and knowing what

family life is like. I mean, I've been married to my dear wife, Mona, a couple hundred years now! And we have close friends, and we know what it is to be family. That's one of the reasons that perhaps you and I can relate -- we are of the same era in music and jazz which we have been involved in, and our wives -- your lady and my lady -- have been so beautiful in enhancing our lives and making it so very comfortable for us, and I think that your lady deserves all the allocades we can say about her.

We're of the same fabric -- everybody isn't coming from a family, if it was broken up at times when I was young. I always wanted a family life, and all those years that I put my dues in, years we haven't even gotten into yet, with the bas$ drum falling off the car in the middle of a blizzard in Iowa, and those things that we haven't delved in yet -- I always wanted a family life, and I've had it. And I have it now.

And we do have it now, and we're enjoying it, and we will digress back to that -- I think that you and I can honestly sit here and say that if it weren't for our wives, things wouldn't be as nice for us now as they are. Do you agree with that?
They get better all the time.
